key_insight: A symmetric semi-implicit projection scheme achieves second-order time accuracy for spherical shallow-water equations while restricting stability only through the explicit advection step.
engineering_relevance: The method supports larger time steps for geophysical flow simulation by subcycling advection without adding implicit wave solves.
method: Use compatible finite elements with DG-upwind SSPRK3 advection and an H(div)-conforming implicit wave discretisation.
Apply symmetric splitting: an explicit half-step, a full advection step, then an implicit half-step that projects velocity into H(div).
Solve the implicit system efficiently through hybridisation in Firedrake.
evidence_signal: Standard spherical shallow-water benchmarks demonstrate second-order convergence, good parallel scaling, and stable results at Courant numbers up to 1 with two advection subcycles and second-order finite elements.
watch_item: Advection substeps must still satisfy their CFL condition; the reported stability results do not establish unrestricted large-time-step accuracy.
paper_title: A Second-Order Semi-Implicit Projection Time-Stepping Scheme for the Shallow-Water Equations on the Sphere Using Compatible Finite Elements
